tagline.en: Turned a Stanford thesis into Google, then stepped out of sight as his fortune kept growing
tagline.zh: 把斯坦福的博士课题做成了 Google，然后淡出公众视野，财富却继续增长

label.zh: Google 上市前股权 + 早期积蓄（估算）

label.en: Wealth outside Alphabet (cash from share sales, real estate, private ventures; estimate)
label.zh: Alphabet 以外的财富（售股所得现金、房产及私人项目，估算）
Alphabet 持股（B 类 + C 类）

t.en: Michigan childhood
t.zh: 密歇根少年

desc.en: Grows up among computers in East Lansing and studies engineering at the University of Michigan
desc.zh: 在东兰辛与电脑为伴长大，在密歇根大学学习工程

t.en: Stanford and BackRub
t.zh: 斯坦福与 BackRub

desc.en: Meets Sergey Brin, turns a thesis on web links into a search engine and writes the PageRank paper
desc.zh: 结识谢尔盖·布林，把关于网页链接的课题做成搜索引擎，写出 PageRank 论文

t.en: Garage to IPO
t.zh: 从车库到上市

desc.en: Founds Google, raises venture money, finds a business in search ads and hands the CEO title to Eric Schmidt
desc.zh: 创立 Google，拿到风险投资，靠搜索广告找到商业模式，并把 CEO 头衔交给埃里克·施密特

t.en: The triumvirate years
t.zh: 三人共治

desc.en: Runs products beside Schmidt and Brin as Google lists, buys Android and YouTube and rides out the 2008 crash
desc.zh: 与施密特、布林共同掌舵，主管产品；Google 上市，收购 Android 和 YouTube，熬过 2008 年的暴跌

t.en: CEO again
t.zh: 重掌帅印

desc.en: Takes back the top job, narrows the product line, buys Motorola and DeepMind and backs long-range bets
desc.zh: 重新出任 CEO，精简产品线，收购摩托罗拉和 DeepMind，支持各种长期项目

t.en: Alphabet
t.zh: Alphabet 时代

desc.en: Creates a holding company above Google while antitrust fines, a Senate no-show and a staff walkout pile up
desc.zh: 在 Google 之上设立控股公司；与此同时，反垄断罚单、缺席参议院听证和员工罢工接连而来

t.en: Out of sight
t.zh: 淡出幕后

desc.en: Leaves management but keeps control; the AI boom lifts his fortune past $300 billion before a sharp fall
desc.zh: 退出管理层但保留控制权；人工智能热潮把他的身家推过 3000 亿美元，随后大幅回落

t.en: Born in Lansing, Michigan
t.zh: 出生于密歇根州兰辛

summary.en: Larry Page was born in Lansing, Michigan, and grew up in neighboring East Lansing in a household full of computers and science magazines. He has said he knew early that he wanted to invent things.
summary.zh: 拉里·佩奇出生在密歇根州兰辛，在相邻的东兰辛长大，家里到处是电脑和科技杂志。他说自己很早就知道长大要搞发明。

why.en: Starting point, not scored. Human capital begins at the average level for a child born in the United States.
why.zh: 起点事件，不计分。人力资本以美国同龄人的平均水平作为初始值。

t.en: Graduates from the University of Michigan and heads to Stanford
t.zh: 从密歇根大学毕业，前往斯坦福读博

summary.en: He earned a bachelor's degree in computer engineering with honors from the University of Michigan, then entered Stanford's computer science PhD program, where he met fellow student Sergey Brin.
summary.zh: 他以优等成绩拿到密歇根大学计算机工程学士学位，随后进入斯坦福大学计算机科学博士项目，在那里认识了同学谢尔盖·布林。

why.en: An education step: the human-capital target rises with a strong engineering degree and a place in a top PhD program. Only the year is confirmed, so the date is year precision.
why.zh: 学历台阶：拿到扎实的工科学位并进入顶尖博士项目，人力资本目标值上调。只能确认年份，因此日期精度为“年”。

t.en: BackRub, the search engine that became Google, runs on Stanford's servers
t.zh: Google 的前身 BackRub 在斯坦福服务器上运行

summary.en: For his doctoral research Page set out to map the links between web pages. With Brin he built BackRub, a search engine that ranked a page by the links pointing to it. An early version was available on Stanford's website by August 1996.
summary.zh: 为了博士课题，佩奇着手梳理网页之间的链接关系。他和布林一起做出了搜索引擎 BackRub，按照指向某个网页的链接来给它排序。到 1996 年 8 月，早期版本已经可以在斯坦福的网站上使用。

why.en: A research project with no market value yet, so financial capital does not move. It is the technical root of everything later, so the reputation coefficient gets a small +1%.
why.zh: 这还只是没有市场价值的研究项目，金融资本不动。但它是后来一切的技术源头，口碑系数小幅 +1%。

t.en: Page and Brin publish the paper describing Google and PageRank
t.zh: 佩奇与布林发表介绍 Google 和 PageRank 的论文

summary.en: The two students published "The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine", which described a prototype called Google and the PageRank method named after Page. It became one of the most cited papers in computer science.
summary.zh: 两位学生发表了论文《大规模超文本网络搜索引擎剖析》，介绍了名为 Google 的原型系统，以及以佩奇名字命名的 PageRank 算法。它后来成为计算机科学领域被引用最多的论文之一。

why.en: Academic credit that no valuation captures at this point, so the reputation coefficient gets +2%.
why.zh: 这是当时任何估值都反映不了的学术声誉，口碑系数 +2%。

t.en: Andy Bechtolsheim writes a $100,000 check to a company that does not exist yet
t.zh: 安迪·贝希托尔斯海姆给尚未成立的公司开出 10 万美元支票

summary.en: Sun Microsystems co-founder Andy Bechtolsheim saw a demo and wrote a $100,000 check made out to "Google Inc." before the company had been incorporated. Other early backers followed within months.
summary.zh: 太阳微系统公司联合创始人安迪·贝希托尔斯海姆看完演示后，开出一张抬头为“Google Inc.”的 10 万美元支票，而当时公司还没有注册。几个月内又有其他早期投资人跟进。

why.en: The first outside money. The stake anchor rises to a small estimated value; the terms of the angel round were never published, so the figure is a rough estimate.
why.zh: 第一笔外部资金。持股价值锚点上调到一个较小的估算值；天使轮的条款从未公开，所以这个数字只是粗略估算。

fin.en: Estimated stake after the angel money: around $1.5 million.
fin.zh: 天使资金到位后的估算持股价值：约 150 万美元。

t.en: Google is incorporated in a Menlo Park garage, with Page as CEO
t.zh: Google 在门洛帕克的一间车库里注册成立，佩奇任 CEO

summary.en: Page and Brin incorporated Google and set up in a garage rented from Susan Wojcicki in Menlo Park, California. Page, then 25, became the first chief executive and both founders put their PhDs on hold.
summary.zh: 佩奇和布林注册成立 Google，在加州门洛帕克向苏珊·沃西基租来的车库里办公。25 岁的佩奇出任首任 CEO，两位创始人都中断了博士学业。

why.en: The turning point of his life: from this day he owns founder equity. Financial capital switches from student savings to an estimated stake value, and human capital starts climbing toward the level of a startup founder.
why.zh: 人生转折点：从这一天起他持有创始人股权。金融资本从学生积蓄切换为估算的股权价值，人力资本开始向“创业公司创始人”的水平爬升。

fin.en: Founder equity enters the model (valued by interpolating between funding events).
fin.zh: 创始人股权进入模型（私有阶段按各次融资事件插值估算）。

t.en: Kleiner Perkins and Sequoia invest $25 million
t.zh: 凯鹏华盈与红杉资本投资 2500 万美元

summary.en: Google announced $25 million in equity funding led by Sequoia Capital and Kleiner Perkins, two rival venture firms that rarely shared a deal. Michael Moritz and John Doerr joined the board.
summary.zh: Google 宣布获得 2500 万美元股权融资，由红杉资本和凯鹏华盈共同领投——这两家互为对手的风投机构很少同投一个项目。迈克尔·莫里茨和约翰·杜尔加入董事会。

why.en: First institutional round. The stake anchor steps up to roughly $16 million. This is an estimate: the valuation was not disclosed and is taken from press reports of about $100 million, times an ownership share of about one sixth.
why.zh: 第一轮机构融资。持股价值锚点上调到约 1600 万美元。这是估算：估值没有披露，这里采用媒体报道的约 1 亿美元，乘以约六分之一的持股比例。

fin.zh: 估算持股价值：约 1600 万美元。

src.name: Google press release · Google Receives $25 Million in Equity Funding (1999-06-07)

t.en: Google launches AdWords, its self-service ad program
t.zh: Google 推出自助广告系统 AdWords

summary.en: Google opened a self-service program that let any business buy small text ads shown next to search results for chosen keywords. About 350 advertisers had tried the test version. Search advertising went on to supply most of the company's revenue.
summary.zh: Google 开放了一套自助广告系统，任何企业都可以购买与特定关键词匹配、显示在搜索结果旁边的小段文字广告。测试阶段约有 350 家广告主试用。搜索广告后来贡献了公司绝大部分收入。

why.en: The moment a popular search engine got a business model. The money shows up in later valuations; the reputation coefficient gets +2% for being CEO when it launched.
why.zh: 这是一款受欢迎的搜索引擎找到商业模式的时刻。收益体现在之后的估值里；作为上线时的 CEO，口碑系数 +2%。

src.name: Google press release · Google Launches Self-Service Advertising Program (2000-10-23)

t.en: Eric Schmidt becomes CEO; Page moves to President, Products
t.zh: 埃里克·施密特出任 CEO，佩奇改任产品总裁

summary.en: At the urging of the company's investors, Google brought in former Novell chief Eric Schmidt as chief executive. Page gave up the CEO title and became President, Products, while Brin became President, Technology. The three ran the company together for the next decade.
summary.zh: 在投资人的推动下，Google 请来前 Novell 掌门人埃里克·施密特担任首席执行官。佩奇交出 CEO 头衔，改任产品总裁，布林任技术总裁。此后十年，三人共同管理公司。

why.en: Scored as mixed: he lost the top title, but the arrangement kept the founders in control and helped the company grow up. No reputation shock.
why.zh: 记为好坏参半：他失去了最高头衔，但这一安排让创始人保住了控制权，也帮助公司走向成熟。不计口碑冲击。

src.name: Google press release · Google Names Dr. Eric Schmidt Chief Executive Officer (2001-08-06)

t.en: Receives the Marconi Prize with Sergey Brin
t.zh: 与布林共同获得马可尼奖

summary.en: Page and Brin were awarded the Marconi Prize, a leading honor in communications engineering, for inventing the Google search engine. The same year Page was elected to the National Academy of Engineering.
summary.zh: 佩奇和布林因发明 Google 搜索引擎获得通信工程领域的重要奖项马可尼奖。同年，佩奇当选美国国家工程院院士。

why.en: A pure reputation event from his engineering peers, so the reputation coefficient gets +2%. Only the year is confirmed.
why.zh: 来自工程界同行的纯声誉事件，口碑系数 +2%。只能确认年份。

t.en: Google files for an IPO with a founders' letter written by Page
t.zh: Google 递交上市申请，附佩奇执笔的创始人公开信

summary.en: Google filed its registration statement with the SEC. It opened with a letter signed by Page and Brin, "An Owner's Manual for Google's Shareholders", which said Google was not a conventional company and explained that a two-class share structure would leave the founders with significant control.
summary.zh: Google 向美国证监会递交注册文件。文件开头是佩奇和布林署名的一封信《Google 股东手册》，信中称 Google 不是一家传统公司，并说明双重股权结构会让创始人保有重大控制权。

why.en: The filing revealed the company's finances for the first time and set the tone for founder-controlled technology listings. The reputation coefficient gets +2%; the value itself arrives with the IPO.
why.zh: 这份文件首次公开了公司的财务状况，也为此后创始人控股的科技公司上市定下了基调。口碑系数 +2%；价值本身随 IPO 体现。

t.en: Google lists on Nasdaq at $85 a share, valued at about $23 billion
t.zh: Google 以每股 85 美元在纳斯达克上市，市值约 230 亿美元

summary.en: Google sold shares through an unusual online auction, raising about $1.67 billion at $85 a share, below the range it first proposed. The stock closed its first day near $100. Page sold a small part of his holding and kept about 38 million shares.
summary.zh: Google 采用少见的网上竞价方式发行股票，以每股 85 美元募资约 16.7 亿美元，定价低于最初提出的区间。首日收盘价接近 100 美元。佩奇卖出了一小部分持股，保留约 3800 万股。

why.en: Anchor switch: from this day financial capital = ownership × shares outstanding × the daily close. His remaining stake of about 14% was worth roughly $3.2 billion at the offer price. The share count is taken from the prospectus and his year-end 2004 ownership filing.
why.zh: 锚点切换：从这一天起，金融资本 = 持股比例 × 总股本 × 当日收盘价。他剩下的约 14% 股份按发行价计算约值 32 亿美元。持股数量依据招股书和他 2004 年底的持股申报文件。

fin.en: Priced daily from the GOOGL quote from here on.
fin.zh: 此后按 GOOGL 日线逐日计价。

src.name: SEC EDGAR · Larry Page Schedule 13G (holdings at 2004-12-31)

t.en: Google buys the startup Android for at least $50 million
t.zh: Google 以至少 5000 万美元收购初创公司 Android

summary.en: Google quietly acquired Android Inc., a small company building software for mobile phones. The first Android phone, the T-Mobile G1, was announced in September 2008, and the system later became the most widely used mobile software in the world.
summary.zh: Google 低调收购了开发手机软件的小公司 Android Inc.。第一款 Android 手机 T-Mobile G1 于 2008 年 9 月发布，这套系统后来成为全球使用最广的移动操作系统。

why.en: Tiny in price and invisible to the market at the time. The long-run value sits in the share price; the reputation coefficient gets +2% for a deal Page backed as head of products. Sources give the month, not the day.
why.zh: 交易金额很小，当时市场几乎没有察觉。长期价值已体现在股价里；这笔交易由时任产品总裁的佩奇支持，口碑系数 +2%。资料只给出月份，没有具体日期。

t.en: Google agrees to buy YouTube for $1.65 billion in stock
t.zh: Google 宣布以 16.5 亿美元股票收购 YouTube

summary.en: Google announced an all-stock deal for YouTube, a video site that was less than two years old and faced copyright complaints. It was Google's largest purchase up to then.
summary.zh: Google 宣布以全股票方式收购 YouTube。这家视频网站成立还不到两年，正面临版权方面的投诉。这是 Google 当时金额最大的一笔收购。

why.en: Questioned as expensive at the time and later seen as a bargain. The value is carried by the share price; a small +1% for the decision by the three-person leadership.
why.zh: 当时被质疑买贵了，后来被认为相当划算。价值由股价体现；三人领导层共同作出这个决定，口碑系数小幅 +1%。

src.name: Google press release · Google To Acquire YouTube for $1.65 Billion in Stock (2006-10-09)

t.en: Shares hit their financial-crisis low, 65% below the 2007 peak
t.zh: 股价触及金融危机低点，较 2007 年高点下跌 65%

summary.en: As the global financial crisis cut advertising budgets, Google's stock closed at its lowest level of the downturn on this day, about 65% under its peak of November 2007. It recovered most of the loss within a year.
summary.zh: 全球金融危机压缩了广告预算，Google 股价在这一天收于本轮下跌的最低点，比 2007 年 11 月的高点低约 65%。一年之内，股价收复了大部分失地。

why.en: A market-wide fall that is fully in the share price, so no reputation shock (rep = 0).
why.zh: 这是全市场的下跌，已完全体现在股价里，不计口碑冲击（rep = 0）。

t.en: Page returns as Google's chief executive after ten years
t.zh: 时隔十年，佩奇重新出任 Google CEO

summary.en: Page took back the chief executive role from Eric Schmidt, who became executive chairman. The change had been announced on January 20. Page reorganized the company around a few product areas and closed dozens of smaller projects.
summary.zh: 佩奇从埃里克·施密特手中接回首席执行官职务，施密特转任执行董事长。这一变动已在 1 月 20 日宣布。佩奇围绕少数几个产品领域重组公司，并关停了数十个小项目。

why.en: Human capital steps up to the level of a chief executive of one of the world's largest companies. The stock barely moved on the day; the reputation coefficient gets +2%.
why.zh: 人力资本上调到“全球最大公司之一的 CEO”的水平。当天股价几乎没有变化；口碑系数 +2%。

src.name: Official Google Blog · An update from the Chairman (2011-01-20)

t.en: Announces the $12.5 billion purchase of Motorola Mobility
t.zh: 宣布以 125 亿美元收购摩托罗拉移动

summary.en: Four months into his term Page announced Google's largest acquisition, mainly to gain Motorola's patents and protect Android from lawsuits. In January 2014 Google agreed to sell the handset business to Lenovo for about $2.9 billion while keeping most of the patents.
summary.zh: 上任四个月后，佩奇宣布了 Google 史上最大的一笔收购，主要目的是拿到摩托罗拉的专利、保护 Android 免受诉讼。2014 年 1 月，Google 同意以约 29 亿美元把手机业务卖给联想，同时保留大部分专利。

why.en: Scored as mixed: the patents had defensive value, but the hardware business was sold at a far lower price. The cost is in the share price, so rep = 0.
why.zh: 记为好坏参半：专利有防御价值，但硬件业务后来以低得多的价格卖出。成本已体现在股价里，rep = 0。

src.name: Official Google Blog · Supercharging Android: Google to Acquire Motorola Mobility (2011-08-15)
Official Google Blog · Lenovo to acquire Motorola Mobility (2014-01-29)

t.en: Google forfeits $500 million over ads for Canadian online pharmacies
t.zh: Google 因加拿大网上药店广告被没收 5 亿美元

summary.en: Google agreed to forfeit $500 million to the U.S. government for having allowed Canadian online pharmacies to advertise prescription drugs to American consumers through AdWords. It was among the largest forfeitures in U.S. history at the time.
summary.zh: Google 同意向美国政府上缴 5 亿美元，原因是它曾允许加拿大网上药店通过 AdWords 向美国消费者投放处方药广告。这在当时是美国历史上金额最大的没收案之一。

why.en: The company had already set the money aside, so the stock did not react. The reputation coefficient takes -1% because it happened in his first months as CEO.
why.zh: 公司此前已为此计提款项，股价没有反应。事情发生在他出任 CEO 的头几个月，口碑系数 -1%。

src.name: U.S. Department of Justice · Google forfeits $500 million (press release)

t.en: Announces a new class of non-voting shares to preserve founder control
t.zh: 宣布增设无投票权股份，以维持创始人控制权

summary.en: Together with quarterly results, Google proposed giving every shareholder one new non-voting Class C share for each share held, in effect a two-for-one split. In a letter Page said the aim was to keep the founders' voting control as new stock was issued. The Class C shares were distributed in April 2014 after a shareholder lawsuit was settled.
summary.zh: 在发布季度财报的同时，Google 提议向每位股东按每股派发一股没有投票权的 C 类新股，效果相当于一拆二。佩奇在信中说，这样做是为了在今后增发股票时保住创始人的投票控制权。一起股东诉讼和解后，C 类股于 2014 年 4 月派发。

why.en: Scored as mixed. His economic stake did not change, so financial capital is unaffected. Governance critics objected to locking in control, so the reputation coefficient takes a small -1%. Share counts in the model are adjusted for this split.
why.zh: 记为好坏参半。他的经济持股没有变化，金融资本不受影响。公司治理方面的批评者反对锁定控制权，口碑系数小幅 -1%。模型中的股本数量已按这次拆股调整。

src.name: New Statesman · Control freaks: Google's stock split (2012-04)
Khaleej Times · Google to split stock to keep power with founders

t.en: Google buys the London AI lab DeepMind
t.zh: Google 收购伦敦人工智能实验室 DeepMind

summary.en: Google confirmed that it was acquiring DeepMind, a small artificial-intelligence research company in London, for a price reported at between $400 million and $650 million. The lab later produced AlphaGo and AlphaFold and became the core of Google's AI work.
summary.zh: Google 确认收购伦敦的小型人工智能研究公司 DeepMind，据报道价格在 4 亿至 6.5 亿美元之间。这家实验室后来做出了 AlphaGo 和 AlphaFold，并成为 Google 人工智能研发的核心。

why.en: Too small to move the stock then. The +2% on the reputation coefficient is for an early bet on AI made while he was CEO; the price was never officially disclosed.
why.zh: 当时金额太小，不足以影响股价。口碑系数 +2% 是因为他在任 CEO 期间较早押注人工智能；收购价格从未正式披露。

t.en: Named Fortune's Businessperson of the Year
t.zh: 当选《财富》杂志年度商业人物

summary.en: Fortune put Page at the top of its annual ranking of business leaders, citing three years of revenue growth above 20% together with long-range projects such as self-driving cars and internet balloons.
